purpose: Bounded source-pinned evidence for a personal adapter that defers nanodot review guidance and corpus ownership to the upstream repository.

canonical_owner.fixture_resolution: All fixture paths in samples are relative to the upstream canonical tests/fixtures/nanodot-review directory; no executable corpus is duplicated here.

snapshot.publication_claim: Public tag and package declarations only; tag existence is not proof of package or release publication.

source_drift.summary: Canonical architecture map still pins 711b45c. Routing and test-quality prose incorrectly describe main as scaffold-only; these are stale guidance claims, not runtime findings.
Main implements comment writes, content-bound capabilities, gated/auto/readonly modes, intent-first recovery and daily write quota. AUTO is default; absent standing grants skip writes.
Main adds provider registry, retry and token-usage persistence, plus digest/stale/flaky watches, task-row quarantine and operational tuning.
DSH integration is a standalone-CLI adapter. Current UI is a loopback shell and /api/health only; screen names are placeholders. CI now declares Python 3.11 and 3.12.

post_tag_merges.summary: Compressed 3000-tick soak test; generous health tripwires, not a benchmark.
Malformed provider-response corpus, era-jump migration test, non-dict payload usage-accounting fixes in both providers.
Loopback UI skeleton and handler-level tests.

canonical_skill_tests.network_boundary: Both-case HTTP/HTTPS/ALL proxy variables pointed to 127.0.0.1:9; NO_PROXY empty. Tests were inspected first; live gh transport mocked and CLI offline fixture paths used.

historical_source_verification.method: Compared all canonical fixture excerpt bytes and full evaluator bytes against local git show at each exact historical SHA/path; checked original SHA256 values.

affected_runtime_tests.command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=src PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_provider_corpus.py tests/test_auto_adversarial.py tests/test_soak.py tests/test_ui_server.py

verification.upstream_worktree: clean before and after audit; no upstream edits or publication performed

historical_pairs.severity_rationale: P2 for the defective sample: a crash/replay with changed optional evidence or text duplicates one durable inbox occurrence, a bounded persistence/delivery reliability regression. This does not establish lost terminal notification, a privacy violation or exactly-once OS-popup behavior; distinct occurrences must remain deliverable.

coverage_limits: The complete canonical corpus has eight samples in four historical families. The two referenced pairs above are curated and unblinded, not a generalized precision/recall evaluation.
Clean labels cover the stated scenario only, not an entire commit or file. Source-hash consistency and exact git-blob matching do not independently establish all adjudication claims.
Historical executable checks use pure excerpts and minimal doubles. CLI stop forwarding is structural; no actual CLI process is executed by the historical corpus.

No full runtime suite, live GitHub/provider calls, OS notification delivery, personal-machine installation, npm bootstrap, browser/server integration, release publication verification or performance benchmark was executed.
UI source tests are handler-level and AST/structural checks. They do not establish actual socket binding or browser operation.
New source paths fall back to inspect-context in the canonical router; passing route tests do not establish dedicated review coverage for writes, quotas, provider registry, DSH or UI.

test_quality_observation.summary: The AUTO derived-capability scope-change test does not establish the claimed race: its standing grant uses watch:s1 while WriteFlow derives watch, no capability is explicitly derived, and the pending-capability loop can be empty. This is a source-inspected coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime defect.
